notes: Held-out questions on the real clone, prepared by hand with read-only git commands (git show/ls-tree/log/tag --contains); no rw.repo output was consulted. Do not edit after any E2/E4 run: changes require a new evaluation retaining the originals.

questions.question: At 2.2.0, trace Serializer.dumps to where the HMAC signature bytes are computed.
questions.expected_answer: Serializer.dumps calls self.dump_payload(obj) then self.make_signer(salt).sign(payload); Signer.sign calls self.get_signature(value); get_signature calls self.algorithm.get_signature(key, value); HMACAlgorithm.get_signature uses hmac.new(key, msg=value, digestmod=self.digest_method).

questions.question: How is the default digest method of Signer defined at 0.24 versus 2.2.0, and why did it change?
questions.expected_answer: 0.24: Signer.default_digest_method = staticmethod(hashlib.sha1) in itsdangerous.py. 2.2.0: default_digest_method = staticmethod(_lazy_sha1), a wrapper that defers hashlib.sha1 access to runtime so FIPS builds without SHA-1 do not fail at import.

questions.question: What happened to the single-module itsdangerous.py, and in which tag?
questions.expected_answer: Commit d4950c0 ('move to src directory') renamed itsdangerous.py to src/itsdangerous/__init__.py; first tag containing it is 1.0.0. 0.24 is the last tag with the top-level itsdangerous.py.

questions.question: Which release first lacks src/itsdangerous/jws.py and why?
questions.expected_answer: 2.1.0. Commit 506ca21 'remove deprecated code' deleted jws.py (JWS functionality; use a library such as Authlib) and the itsdangerous.json shim; 2.0.1 is the last tag with jws.py.

questions.question: Which source files under src/ changed between 2.0.1 and 2.1.0?
questions.expected_answer: __init__.py, _json.py, encoding.py, jws.py (deleted), serializer.py and url_safe.py; the bulk is jws.py removal (259 lines) and the _json shim reduction.

questions.question: Commit 3edfbbb handled OverflowError in timed unsign on 32-bit systems. Which tag first contains it and what does the handler catch?
questions.expected_answer: First tag 2.1.2. TimestampSigner.unsign catches (ValueError, OSError, OverflowError) and raises BadTimeSignature; in 2.1.1 it catches only (ValueError, OSError).

questions.question: Commit 37f0997 ('catching year overflow ValueError') - which tag first contains it?
Merge commit 64cd581 (PR #299): what are its parents and which tag first contains it?
questions.expected_answer: Parents faa28bc (first) and 3edfbbb (PR branch, the 32-bit OverflowError fix); first tag 2.1.2.

questions.question: How is __version__ provided at 2.2.0 compared with 0.24?
questions.expected_answer: 2.2.0: a module __getattr__ in __init__.py emits a DeprecationWarning and returns importlib.metadata.version('itsdangerous'). At 0.24 itsdangerous.py defines no __version__ attribute.

questions.question: At 2.2.0, what does `loads` do?
questions.expected_answer: Ambiguous: Serializer.loads (verify signature then load payload), TimedSerializer.loads (adds max_age), the _json helper loads, and the protocol stub in serializer.py. A correct answer lists candidates or asks.

questions.question: At 2.2.0, which class implements RSA/asymmetric signatures?
questions.expected_answer: No evidence: 2.2.0 has only HMACAlgorithm and NoneAlgorithm; no asymmetric signing. Correct answer reports absence.
